issue.title: Fix the sase-ct flake class at its root - process-global state leaking between tests
issue.description: The tests behind sase-ct stop failing under the full parallel lane because the process-global state that leaks between tests is fixed by mechanism, a leak detector gate makes the class non-recurring, tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt shrinks to only nodes proven still broken, and sase-ct, sase-iy.5, sase-j4, sase-j5, and sase-j6 are closed on evidence.

issue.title: Fix the confirmed xprompt VCS-tag cache leak
issue.description: vcs-cache - give the caches derived from workspace-provider metadata a real invalidation entry point and restore them on teardown, so a test that fakes plugin metadata stops poisoning every later test in its worker.

issue.title: Build a global-state leak detector and inventory every leak in the suite
issue.description: leak-detector - build an opt-in pytest plugin that snapshots process-global state around every test, distinguishes cache warming from poisoning, and delivers a full-suite inventory artifact of every leak. Reports only; blocks nothing.

issue.title: Stop the flake gate from flagging node IDs that no longer exist
issue.description: stale-nodes - bead sase-j5. Make the reproducible-flake gate skip or separately report recorded node IDs absent from the collected suite, so a renamed test stops manufacturing pressure to bump the baseline cutoff.

issue.title: Fix every inventoried leak and root-cause the residual flakes
issue.description: fix-leaks - fix every poisoning leak in the inventory by mechanism, deterministically reproduce and fix the bead-cluster and plan-approval nodes whose cause is not yet known, and flip the leak detector into a blocking gate so the class cannot recur.

issue.title: Shrink the baseline, run the exit criteria, and close the beads
issue.description: retire - remove every fixed node from the flake baseline, run the four exit criteria non-vacuously on the combined tree, and close sase-j4, sase-j5, sase-j6, sase-ct, and sase-iy.5 on that evidence.

payload.entry: Added collectible_nodeid_oracle (AST-based, per-file memoised) to tests/_test_selection_health.py; reproducible_flake_nodeids now excludes stale (uncollectable) node IDs and the new stale_flake_nodeids reports them separately. Added unresolved_commit_order_count to surface heads git_commit_order_oracle cannot resolve. Wired both into tools/selection_health's --explain/gate output. New unit tests (tests/test_test_selection_health_correlation.py) and CLI tests (tests/test_selection_health_tool.py) cover: a recorded-but-uncollectable node is reported as stale, not a live flake; unresolved commit-order heads are counted. Verified: just check green (all lint gates + scoped test lane); targeted pytest run of the 3 touched test files all pass (65 tests); just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake still non-vacuously flags a live reproducible flake (tests/test_bead/test_plus_one_presentation.py::test_post_close_plus_one_badge_marker_search_and_json_agree, the sase-j6 node) - confirmed via git stash that this same flake and exit code reproduce identically on unmodified master, so it is pre-existing debt explicitly scoped to the epic's later fix-leaks phase, not introduced or masked by this change.

Fixed the confirmed xprompt VCS-tag cache leak (vcs-cache phase): added sase.workspace_provider.reset_workflow_metadata_caches() as the single invalidation entry point clearing get_all_workflow_metadata plus all derived caches (both mirrored _VCS_TAG_PATTERN/_VCS_TAG_EMBEDDED_PATTERN/_VCS_REPLACE_PATTERN copies, _VCS_UNDERSCORE_NORMALIZER, _LAUNCH_XPROMPT_AT_REF_RE, and renamed _workflow_names -> known_workflow_names); made tests/_workspace_provider_helpers.py's patch_*_metadata restore on monkeypatch teardown (not just setup) via a _TeardownResetTrigger that fires reset_workflow_metadata_caches() on both patch and undo; added an autouse snapshot/restore backstop fixture in tests/conftest.py. Verified: both plan reproduction commands pass (poisoner tests/test_removed_hg_workspace_workflow.py followed by each of the three previously-poisoned victims), new tests/test_workspace_metadata_cache_teardown.py regression test passes now and was confirmed to fail on the parent commit, and 'just check' is green (14/14 gates, scoped test lane escalated to the full suite because tests/conftest.py changed).

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: make the leak-detector flag available to no-path pytest invocations — the option is registered from tests/conftest.py, so tools/run_pytest fast --sase-detect-global-leaks needs an explicit tests path unless a safely importable early plugin path is added.

Implemented reporting-only --sase-detect-global-leaks pytest detector with xdist aggregation and warm/poison classification; calibration on tests/test_removed_hg_workspace_workflow.py reported the known _VCS_TAG_PATTERN leak; full inventory via tools/run_pytest fast tests passed 28535/10 skipped and wrote file:explicit:ef5ff8dd23bb954daa8c0c7d (4934 poisoning changes across 2118 tests, 36331 warming filtered); just check passed and escalated to the full suite.
Implemented opt-in pytest global-state leak detector; calibration caught _VCS_TAG_PATTERN; full inventory passed (28535 passed, 10 skipped); just check passed.

DISCOVERED ISSUE (2026-08-13, workspace sase_11): tests/test_multi_prompt_launcher_xprompt_groups.py::test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch failed under the full parallel scoped lane with a process-global reserved-name leak -- the class this epic owns.

  just check -> 2 failed, 6507 passed, 3 skipped in 208.57s
  E  sase.agent.launch_validation.AgentNameLaunchCollisionError: Agent name 'research.0.cdx' is taken. Try 'research.0.cdx1'.
  src/sase/agent/launch_validation.py:315

The colliding name 'research.0.cdx' is a REAL agent name from this machine's name registry, not a fixture name, so get_reserved_agent_names() (src/sase/agent/names/_registry.py:80 -> _registry_queries.py:41, load_name_registry()) read ambient registry state that leaked into the test. The node passes immediately in isolation (1 passed in 1.68s) and passed again in a 4-worker run of that file plus tests/monitor/ (100 passed in 4.61s).

Why this belongs here and not on a new task: sase-ct is a retired umbrella that forbids +1, and this exact node was already recorded against it by sase-hj on 2026-08-08 as a known tracked flake ('failed exactly ... test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch after 16,491 passed, then that node passed immediately in isolation'). It is NOT in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, which today lists only sase-jb's and sase-j6's nodes -- so phase sase-j7.5's baseline shrink did not account for it.

Caveat on evidence weight: this is one occurrence. I did not run just test-contention to re-measure, and the same node passed in the clean-tree 'just test' run I did for unrelated triage (that run failed only tests/main/test_project_handler_list_show.py::TestListAndShow::test_project_handler_imports_in_fresh_interpreter, corroborated on ready task sase-kw). Recording the exact collision string here because it names the leaking mechanism precisely -- the agent-name registry -- which the earlier sase-ct-era reports did not.
